transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-14
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~47m
Recording: enabled
Attendees: Marcus Chen, Sofia Alvarez, Tom Nguyen, Jade Patel (Redwood); Nisha Rao, Liam O'Connor, Ethan Park, Maya Singh, Olaf Berg (StellarWorks)

Summary:
Quick partner introduction + discovery for StellarWorks acting as an edge GPU reseller/integrator for Redwood Dedicated & Private. Topics: go-to-market model, margins, partner enablement, technical fit for on-prem / edge, networking and KMS concerns, pilot candidate and next steps.

Topics (auto): partner model; reseller discounts and co-sell; private deployment network constraints; capacity planning; security / compliance asks; partner onboarding timeline

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Marcus Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time today. quick roll call - marcus from redwood, sofia and tom with me, jade's on partner ops - who do we have on the stellarworks side?
00:12 Nisha Rao: hi this is nisha, vp partnerships at stellarworks, thanks for the invite. liam, ethan, maya and olaf are here as well.
00:18 Liam O'Connor: morning, yeah good to meet you all.
00:22 Marcus Chen: awesome. maybe i'll kick off with 2 min of context on why we thought to connect - we've been doing a lot of work enabling dedicated and private deployments for channel partners who want to resell GPU-backed inference as a managed offering. curious about your go-to-market and technical constraints.
01:01 Nisha Rao: perfect. high level — stellarworks sells edge GPU appliances to telco and industrial customers, and we want to bundle inference + managed ops, not just hardware. we looked at a few runtimes, but we're prioritizing a partner who can provide unified API, per-tenant isolation and a channel pricing model.
01:23 Sofia Alvarez: thanks, that's helpful. two quick clarifying q's — 1) are you planning to rebrand the service as StellarWorks managed LLM, or co-branded? and 2) is tenant isolation per customer on the same HU (host unit) or full physical separation required?
01:37 Nisha Rao: good q. likely co-branded initially, with StellarWorks managing first-line support. for isolation we have a mix — some customers require strict physical separation (esp regulated infra), others are ok with logical multi-tenancy.
01:52 Tom Nguyen: got it. from a redwood side our Dedicated pools and Private deployments can do both patterns — dedicated nodes per tenant, or strict VPC-tenant mapping. physical separation will affect margin and minimum commit.
02:10 Ethan Park: quick technical — we run a mix of Jetson-class devices for small inference + A100 racks for higher throughput. interest is in the A100 class offload for large-gen models. how does redwood hand off to local inference vs hosted?
02:28 Marcus Chen: good question. we support smart routing — policy-based. you can route by latency SLO, cost, or region. for edge we often route small models to local device and burst or fall back to Dedicated capacity in partner's site or redwood-hosted Dedicated depending on contract.
03:03 Maya Singh: can you clarify "Dedicated in partner's site" — so we can host the redwood runtime on our racks and sell it?
03:12 Jade Patel: yes; the Private deployment package is our private control plane + runtime that can run in partner-managed VPC or on prem. partners can resell either as a managed service or as a licensed on-prem product depending on enterprise terms.
03:31 Olaf Berg: network egress — customers ask about no data leaving the country. if we host locally, how much telemetry does Redwood pull back into your cloud?
03:44 Marcus Chen: for Private deployments telemetry is opt-in. we ship an ops-agent for metrics and you can opt to forward only health telemetry or none. for enterprise we support on-prem audit logs and optional remote collection via encrypted channels; there is also KMS integration — you can use your KMS/HSM.
04:12 Nisha Rao: good. on the commercial side — what kind of channel margins are typical? we need a model that supports hardware, managed ops, and software fees.
04:23 Marcus Chen: we have a reseller program — baseline margins vary by commit and geography. for Dedicated/reseller we do a two-part split: a discounted SW rate (per-token or per-inference unit) and a reseller margin on the managed services add-on. i'll follow-up with a spreadsheet (we'll itemize MSRP, partner discount tiers, MR and co-sell incentives).
04:50 Liam O'Connor: do you have an established channel agreement or can we customize? our lawyers will want white-label terms and support SLAs.
04:59 Jade Patel: we use a standard partner agreement and can add amendments for white-labeling, but we typically keep a minimum set of SLAs. custom terms are possible for strategic partners.
05:10 Ethan Park: technical deep dive — what's the minimum hardware spec to run a quantized Llama-2 13B at reasonable latency?
05:19 Tom Nguyen: rough ballpark — a single A100 40GB can serve moderate throughput with 2–4 concurrent sessions at 1 token per 40 ms depending on batching. quantization helps a lot; we also recommend KV cache tuning. we have profiles in our docs but i'd like to run model tuning with your actual workload.
05:48 Ethan Park: ok that'll help. we need to test both offline and in-situ. does redwood support continuous batching on edge nodes?
05:56 Tom Nguyen: yes — the runtime supports continuous batching and prefix/KV cache to reduce per-token cost. on the edge we tune thresholds to meet latency SLOs.
06:12 Nisha Rao: from a go-to-market viewpoint, we're also interested in co-marketing, case studies, and joint sales plays. are there partner enablement kits?
06:21 Jade Patel: we have partner portal content — enablement slide decks, product one-pagers, technical onboarding guide, and a sandbox trial for partners. we'll invite you today and drop the partner checklist.
06:33 Marcus Chen: also we typically do a 2-3 week enablement workshop and a pilot framework — quick win is to identify a single pilot customer where you manage hardware + run our private runtime.
06:49 Liam O'Connor: perfect. timeline question — how long from agreement to pilot?
06:54 Sophia Alvarez: depends on physical hardware and network access; for a private deployment on partner racks expect 4-8 weeks for provisioning and integration. for a hosted proof-of-concept we can do something in 1–2 weeks.
07:12 Ethan Park: security — SOC 2, ISO, RBAC, SSO options?
07:18 Marcus Chen: Redwood has SOC 2 and options for enterprise compliance pack; we support SAML/SSO, RBAC and per-route audit logs. for Private deployments audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM and KMS integration is customer-managed.
07:35 Nisha Rao: great. any restrictions on rebranding or white labeling? some vendors limit how partners present service.
07:41 Jade Patel: we generally support co-branding. white-label is allowed for strategic partners with certain contractual conditions. we'll note that for follow-up.
07:53 Maya Singh: curious about pricing granularity — per-token vs per-request — how do we bill when we resell?
07:59 Marcus Chen: we can bill in a few ways: per-token, per-inference unit, or reserved capacity (monthly commit). partners often mix: a reserved baseline plus overage per-token. we'll include examples in the spreadsheet.
08:20 Liam O'Connor: can we surface pricing via our billing platform? do you support reseller invoices or direct billing?
08:27 Jade Patel: we support partner invoicing and can integrate with reseller billing flows. there's a minimal implementation lead time.
08:35 Nisha Rao: on the ops side — upgrades and rollouts — if we host on-prem how do rollouts and canary deploys work? we need predictable maintenance windows.
08:45 Tom Nguyen: the console supports rollouts (canary/A-B) and automatic fallback policies. for private installs, we push a containerized runtime and orchestrator. partner can choose automatic or manual rollouts; we recommend staged canaries.
09:03 Ethan Park: do you push kernel-level updates or is it all containerized?
09:07 Tom Nguyen: mostly containerized; low-level kernel optimizations are optional and may require host OS changes which we'll coordinate.
09:17 Olaf Berg: latency — can you give an example of latency numbers for 2k token context on A100 vs local Jetson?
09:24 Tom Nguyen: rough example: A100 80ms per token (depends on model and batching), local Jetson for smaller models ~200–500ms per token. again quantization and batching change this a lot. we'll make a benchmark sheet.
09:45 Marcus Chen: i'm noting action items — we'll share pricing, partner onboarding sheet and schedule the tech deep-dive.
10:01 Nisha Rao: need to check internal sales motion — for pilot we'd prefer to identify an existing customer who needs an on-prem inference stack. liaise with liam; he'll follow up.
10:12 Liam O'Connor: yes i'll sync with account team and pick two pilot candidates.
10:17 Maya Singh: do you have case studies for telco / industrial that we can show?
10:21 Marcus Chen: we have a telco case study that covers latency and cost savings; i'll send a redacted PDF.
10:29 Ethan Park: one more technical ask — encryption in transit for model weights when cached on edge nodes?
10:35 Tom Nguyen: model weights at rest on edge are encrypted and we support encrypted KV cache; we can integrate with your HSM for key management.
10:43 Nisha Rao: good. also curious about support SLAs — we need 24x7 escalation for premium customers.
10:49 Jade Patel: SLA tiers are in our partner pack; premium support can be added to reseller offerings.
10:55 Liam O'Connor: what about reporting and cost attribution per customer — we need token-level cost breakdown?
11:02 Sofia Alvarez: yes — the console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route/model and per-tenant cost reports. that helps your billing reconciliation.
11:15 Olaf Berg: how do you handle model licensing? if a customer wants a closed-source model or custom weights, can we deploy it?
11:22 Marcus Chen: you can bring-your-own-models in Private deployments and we support custom model onboarding; licensing terms vary and we'll coordinate legal.
11:34 Nisha Rao: ok wrapping up we're aligned on three things: 1) need pricing/margin spreadsheet, 2) schedule tech deep-dive, 3) partner portal invite + onboarding checklist.
11:50 Marcus Chen: yep — i'll drop those items. any blockers on your side?
12:00 Nisha Rao: internal approvals, but no technical blocker yet. we'll aim for pilot candidate by friday.
12:08 Liam O'Connor: i'll confirm names and ping you.
12:13 Marcus Chen: great. final Q — any competitor traps we should call out?
12:18 Nisha Rao: two things — some vendors force vendor-managed hosting with no private option; others lock partners out of key metrics. we want flexibility.
12:30 Marcus Chen: understood. we'll make sure the partner terms show the private/private telemetry options and keys.
12:36 Maya Singh: can you send an example partner contract?
12:40 Jade Patel: yes we'll include it in the follow-up packet.
12:45 Marcus Chen: sweet. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and portal invite.
12:50 Nisha Rao: thanks, bye.
